title: COPD, respiratory failure and home oxygen
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's chronic lung disease and any respiratory failure or oxygen dependence.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for chronic respiratory issues.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 51-year-old male with a known history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He reports persistent shortness of breath that is managed with consistent use of home oxygen. He denies any new chest pain or sudden changes in his baseline oxygen saturation. He reports adherence to his current maintenance medications and reports that his symptoms remain stable compared to his last evaluation.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 92% on 2L home oxygen, RR 18.

Recent Labs: 
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^3/uL
eGFR: 82 mL/min/1.73m2

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
Respiratory: Positive for chronic shortness of breath. Negative for productive cough or wheezing.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or chest pain.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness or syncope.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Social History: Patient works as a warehouse supervisor. He is a former smoker (quit 5 years ago). He denies current alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History: Father had hypertension; Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Medication List:
1. Tiotropium (Spiriva) 18mcg inhaled
2. Salmeterol/Fluticasone inhaler
3. Home oxygen (continuous use)

Exam:
General: Well-appearing male in no acute distress.
Respiratory: Tachypneic but stable. Decreased breath sounds in bilateral lower lobes. No wheezing noted.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard clearly. No murmurs.
Extremities: No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, stable.
2. Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia.

Plan:
1. Continue current maintenance medications as prescribed.
2. Continue home oxygen at current flow rate to address hypoxemic state.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine evaluation.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia: J96.11 (HCC 213), plus Z99.81 for the home oxygen.

distractors.why: The provider diagnoses chronic respiratory failure: J96.11 (HCC 213).
Only chronic respiratory failure is documented.
